relevance: Defines the diagnostic active-site motif AYXCSFR and operon structures that biochemically separate authentic atmospheric CO-oxidizing Form I CoxL from non-scavenging Form II homologs.
title: Distribution, diversity and ecology of aerobic CO-oxidizing bacteria

cr_title: Land-use influences the distribution and activity of high affinity CO-oxidizing bacteria associated to type I-coxL genotype in soil
relevance: Demonstrates that soil atmospheric CO consumption kinetics are driven specifically by Type I coxL genotypes and can vary independently from general soil microbial biomass.
title: Land-use influences the distribution and activity of high affinity CO-oxidizing bacteria associated to type I-coxL genotype in soil

cr_title: Reconstructing Genomes of Carbon Monoxide Oxidisers in Volcanic Deposits Including Members of the Class Ktedonobacteria
relevance: Confirms that Form I CoxL genes are distributed across phylogenetically divergent uncultivated lineages in arid soils, supporting functional redundancy of CO oxidation.
title: Reconstructing Genomes of Carbon Monoxide Oxidisers in Volcanic Deposits Including Members of the Class Ktedonobacteria

cr_title: Benchmarking Community-Wide Estimates of Growth Potential from Metagenomes Using Codon Usage Statistics
relevance: Benchmarks gRodon v2 metagenome mode and highlights GC-bias vulnerabilities and assembly requirements that can obscure correlations between predicted community growth rates and niche traits.
title: Benchmarking Community-Wide Estimates of Growth Potential from Metagenomes Using Codon Usage Statistics

cr_title: Growth rate is a dominant factor predicting the rhizosphere effect
relevance: Finds that predicted maximal growth rate is the primary driver of rhizosphere enrichment across global soil MAGs, directly challenging our finding that growth rate explains only a minor part of root-adjacent shifts.
title: Growth rate is a dominant factor predicting the rhizosphere effect

cr_title: The Systemic Imprint of Growth and Its Uses in Ecological (Meta)Genomics
relevance: Establishes that ribosomal codon usage bias captures life-history maximal growth rate potential rather than instantaneous realized in situ replication rates.
title: The systemic imprint of growth and its uses in ecological (meta)genomics

cr_title: Microbiome Datasets Are Compositional: And This Is Not Optional
relevance: Demonstrates that relative abundance data inherently produce false-positive negative correlations due to constant-sum constraints, necessitating single-copy normalisation or log-ratios.
title: Microbiome Datasets Are Compositional: And This Is Not Optional

cr_title: Relative and Quantitative Rhizosphere Microbiome Profiling Results in Distinct Abundance Patterns
relevance: Shows that per-cell relative profiling produces spurious apparent depletion of soil oligotrophs in the rhizosphere due to copiotroph biomass expansion, warning that 1l loss could be a compositional artifact.
title: Relative and Quantitative Rhizosphere Microbiome Profiling Results in Distinct Abundance Patterns

cr_title: Guidelines for preventing and reporting contamination in low-biomass microbiome studies
relevance: Outlines international consensus standards for negative control sequencing, batch-effect reporting, and bioinformatic filtering specifically in low-biomass environments like hyperarid soils.
title: Guidelines for preventing and reporting contamination in low-biomass microbiome studies

cr_title: Simple statistical identification and removal of contaminant sequences in marker-gene and metagenomics data
relevance: Develops the statistical frequency and prevalence algorithms implemented in decontam to systematically remove reagent and environmental contaminant reads from low-biomass metagenomes.
title: Simple statistical identification and removal of contaminant sequences in marker-gene and metagenomics data

cr_title: Saudi Rainfall (SaRa): hourly 0.1° gridded rainfall (1979–present) for Saudi Arabia via machine learning fusion  of satellite and model data
relevance: Demonstrates that reanalysis precipitation products including ERA5 perform poorly (median KGE 0.21) across Saudi Arabia due to acute gauge scarcity, cautioning against using ERA5 rainfall as ground truth in hyperarid sites.
title: Saudi Rainfall (SaRa): hourly 0.1° gridded rainfall (1979–present) for Saudi Arabia via machine learning fusion of satellite and model data

cr_title: Evaluation of Reanalysis and Satellite Products against Ground-Based Observations in a Desert Environment
relevance: Evaluates ERA5 and ERA5-Land directly against in situ meteorological stations in the hyperarid Rub' al-Khali (WISE-UAE campaign), finding substantial surface biases and limitations in resolving arid land-atmosphere interactions.
title: Evaluation of Reanalysis and Satellite Products against Ground-Based Observations in a Desert Environment

cr_title: Assessment of global precipitation measurement satellite products over Saudi Arabia
relevance: Documents substantial discrepancies in gridded precipitation products across Saudi Arabia and highlights the observational data vacuum in the hyperarid Empty Quarter.
title: Assessment of candidate global precipitation measurement satellite products over Saudi Arabia

cr_title: A species’ response to spatial climatic variation does not predict its response to climate change
cr_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Demonstrates that spatial climate gradients systematically fail to predict dynamic temporal responses to climatic variation, directly supporting the manuscript finding that space-for-time substitution fails between expeditions.
title: A species' response to spatial climatic variation does not predict its response to climate change

cr_title: Rainfall-induced microbial resuscitation reveals functional decoupling across biocrust succession
relevance: Shows using BONCAT-FACS that translational activity upon hydration is decoupled from total community composition, challenging the assumption that metagenomic gene capacity directly reflects in situ activity or flux.
title: Rainfall-induced microbial resuscitation reveals functional decoupling across biocrust succession

cr_title: Intensifying Aridity Undermines the Role of Soil Biodiversity in Supporting Ecosystem Stability
relevance: Finds that intensifying aridity decouples plant productivity (NDVI) from soil microbial stability relationships, aligning with the manuscript finding that plant-carbon proxies explain only a minor part of functional variation.
title: Intensifying aridity undermines the role of soil biodiversity in supporting ecosystem stability

cr_title: Increases in aridity lead to drastic shifts in the assembly of dryland complex microbial networks
relevance: Shows that increasing aridity drives the collapse of mesic plant-associated microbial modules and promotes xeric-adapted oligotrophic modules, providing network-level support for bulk-soil group 1l enrichment with aridity.
title: Increases in aridity lead to drastic shifts in the assembly of dryland complex microbial networks

cr_title: Genomic Features Predict Bacterial Life History Strategies in Soil, as Identified by Metagenomic Stable Isotope Probing
relevance: Establishes how genomic traits such as codon usage bias and operon counts predict carbon responsiveness versus slow-growing oligotrophic survival, providing mechanistic backing for gRodon-derived copiotrophy interpretations.
title: Genomic features predict bacterial life history strategies in soil, as identified by metagenomic stable isotope probing

cr_title: Microbial life-history strategies and genomic traits between pristine and cropland soils
relevance: Demonstrates that carbon-poor soils favor oligotrophic genomic traits that are rapidly selected against upon organic carbon input, illuminating why root-adjacent soils lose specialized group 1l scavengers.
title: Microbial life-history strategies and genomic traits between pristine and cropland soils

cr_title: Divergent soil organic carbon accrual from plant and microbial sources across ecosystem types in a hyper-arid oasis-desert ecotone
relevance: Shows that plant root inputs in hyperarid soils create localized carbon accrual zones that diverge strongly from surrounding desert sands, setting the edaphic contrast between root-adjacent and bulk soils.
title: Divergent soil organic carbon accrual from plant and microbial sources across ecosystem types in a hyper-arid oasis-desert ecotone

cr_title: Diversity and ecological drivers of rhizospheric and endophytic microbiomes of desert plants in king Salman reserve, Saudi Arabia
cr_journal: Journal of King Saud University – Science
relevance: Demonstrates that root systems of wild desert shrubs across Saudi Arabian arid reserves exert strong selective filtering on soil bacteria, providing regional rhizosphere baseline data.
title: Diversity and ecological drivers of rhizospheric and endophytic microbiomes of desert plants in king Salman reserve, Saudi Arabia

cr_title: Microbiome Studies from Saudi Arabia over the Last 10 Years: Achievements, Gaps, and Future Directions
relevance: Identifies the Rub' al-Khali as one of the least characterized desert biomes in Saudi Arabia and highlights the absence of large-scale shotgun metagenomic surveys in the southern desert.
title: Microbiome Studies from Saudi Arabia over the Last 10 Years: Achievements, Gaps, and Future Directions

cr_title: Aeolian Prokaryotic Communities of the Global Dust Belt Over the Red Sea
relevance: Profiles prokaryotic assemblages transported by dust across the Arabian desert dust belt, showing that aeolian dispersal provides a regional taxon pool while local aridity shapes edaphic retention.
title: Aeolian Prokaryotic Communities of the Global Dust Belt Over the Red Sea

cr_title: Summertime dust storms over the Arabian Peninsula and impacts on radiation, circulation, cloud development and rain
relevance: Details convective dust storm mechanisms and radiation alterations over the Rub' al-Khali, linking regional atmospheric dynamics to periodic mineral and nutrient depositions across Empty Quarter dunes.
title: Summertime dust storms over the Arabian Peninsula and impacts on radiation, circulation, cloud development and rain

cr_title: Short-Term Responses of Soil Microbial Communities to Changes in Air Temperature, Soil Moisture and UV Radiation
relevance: Shows that extreme UV and temperature fluctuations directly filter surface microbial communities, providing abiotic justification for sampling distinct depth profiles (0 cm surface vs 5-10 cm bulk).
title: Short-Term Responses of Soil Microbial Communities to Changes in Air Temperature, Soil Moisture and UV Radiation

cr_title: An Unusual Inverted Saline Microbial Mat Community in an Interdune Sabkha in the Rub' al Khali (the Empty Quarter), United Arab Emirates
relevance: Provides direct empirical evidence of extreme geomorphological microhabitat partitioning between dune sands and interdune sabkhas within the hyperarid Rub' al-Khali.
title: An Unusual Inverted Saline Microbial Mat Community in an Interdune Sabkha in the Rub' al Khali (the Empty Quarter), United Arab Emirates

cr_title: Coping with stress the C. crescentus way
relevance: Highlights that DNA-based metagenomic gene counts capture dormant and relic cells in arid soils, cautioning that genomic capacity significantly overestimates active atmospheric gas uptake.
title: Evaluation of rRNA and DNA as biomarkers for microbial activity

cr_title: Genomic evidence for aerotrophy as a defining trait of Ktedonobacteria inhabiting silica-rich oligotrophic caves
relevance: Provides 2026 genomic evidence that atmospheric trace gas scavenging is a deeply conserved trait defining specific oligotrophic bacterial classes, implying that loss of 1l near roots reflects lineage exclusion rather than gene-specific loss.
title: Genomic evidence for aerotrophy as a defining trait of Ktedonobacteria inhabiting silica-rich oligotrophic caves

cr_title: Methods to account for spatial autocorrelation in the analysis of species distributional data: a review
relevance: Warns that spatial autocorrelation inflates type I error rates and shifts coefficient estimates in environmental regressions, demanding explicit spatial modeling before attributing gene copy variation across sites to ERA5 MAP.
title: Methods to account for spatial autocorrelation in the analysis of species distributional data: a review

cr_title: Increasing aridity reduces soil microbial diversity and abundance in global drylands
cr_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Demonstrates that aridity gradients across global drylands drive coordinated shifts in major bacterial phyla, indicating that aridity-hydrogenase correlations are likely mediated by broader taxonomic turnover rather than direct niche selection.
title: Increasing aridity reduces soil microbial diversity and abundance in global drylands

cr_title: Structure and Functions of the Bacterial Microbiota of Plants
relevance: Details the two-step selection model where root exudates systematically enrich fast-growing copiotrophs and deplete oligotrophic taxa, supporting a compositional artefact explanation for group 1l reduction.
title: Structure and functions of the rhizosphere microbiome

cr_title: Molecular Hydrogen, a Neglected Key Driver of Soil Biogeochemical Processes
relevance: Synthesizes how high-affinity hydrogen oxidation activity in soils is regulated post-transcriptionally by moisture and carbon rather than simply matching gene abundance, challenging gene copy counts as pure capacity proxies.
title: Molecular Hydrogen, a Neglected Key Driver of Soil Biogeochemical Processes
